It holds about $1.8 billion in Space Force contracts for 36 satellites meant to spot hypersonic missiles for Golden Dome, with more than 70 on order. 

It's one of the military's biggest suppliers of battlefield radios and jamming gear. 

It also owns Aerojet Rocketdyne, which makes the rocket motors inside America's interceptors.

Nobody is saying today was anything but a mistake.

But think about what one update did to every airport in the country, then look at that list again.

posts.text:
San Diego County named her one of its best teachers. Three years later she stood in a courtroom in jail clothes, crying, and read this out loud:

"I ripped away their childhood."

Two of her students. Boys, 11 and 12. Neither one had social media, so she used what the school had already put in their hands: their classroom tablets.

Her name is Jacqueline Ma. Fifth and sixth grade, Lincoln Acres Elementary, National City, California. Teacher of the Year, 2022.

According to the detective who testified, she bought the boys clothes and gaming gear. She messaged them on the school tablets and inside a video game chat. She told one of them to delete everything, or switch to a mode where messages vanish on their own. With the 12-year-old, it didn't stay on a screen.

It wasn't the school that caught her. A mother did. She picked up the family tablet, read the messages and went to police. Ma was arrested in March 2023 and never walked free again.

She was charged with 18 felonies and faced more than 160 years to life. The judge called the evidence "overwhelmingly clear." In February 2025 she pleaded guilty to four counts, including lewd acts on a child under 14.

May 9, 2025: 30 years to life. No parole hearing until she has served every single one of those 30 years.

In the video below, she reads her apology at sentencing. Boys that age, she says, should be "playing outside, feeling carefree." The boys weren't in the room to hear it.

A Teacher of the Year, a school-issued tablet, and it took a mother, not the school, to see what was happening. Should the district answer for this too?

posts.text:
Marvin Gaye's divorce deal gave his ex-wife the first $600,000 from his next album. So he made the whole album about her

Then he invited her to the studio to listen

She was getting paid for every song on it. After the album came out, she considered suing him over those songs for $5 million

But she wasn't just his ex-wife

She was the older sister of his boss, Motown founder Berry Gordy. The man who owned the label that would put out the album

In the video below, 1983, Marvin explains how he works: "If I'm being divorced, I write divorce albums"

Her name was Anna Gordy. When they married in 1963, he was a young singer at her brother's label. She was 17 years older

Twelve years later she filed for divorce and asked for $1 million

A judge ordered him to pay $5,500 a month until it was settled. He fell behind. A warrant was issued for his arrest

He was broke and owed back taxes. So his lawyer came up with a strange deal

Anna would get $600,000. The advance on his next album, plus the royalties after that

The plan was a quick record. Get it done, get her paid

Instead he spent more than a year in his own studio and made a double album. Almost every song about the marriage. Why it started, why it ended, whose fault it was

He called it "Here, My Dear"

It flopped. It didn't even earn back the advance

So Marvin, by then bankrupt, had to keep sending her checks every month to cover the rest

Decades later Rolling Stone put it on its list of the 500 greatest albums of all time

The case for Anna: she asked for $1 million, settled for $600,000, and he was the one who stopped paying

Should your ex get paid from work you do after the divorce?
